event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: ON’s 2022 10-K frames COVID-19 as both a realized and continuing enterprise-wide threat.  The risk discussions move well beyond boiler-plate language: management acknowledges that the pandemic has already disrupted operations, supply chains and financial results, and it catalogs concrete mechanisms—worker absenteeism, port closures, labor shortages, variant resurgence—that could prolong or deepen the impact.  The filing therefore mixes backward-looking evidence ("have had" material effects) with forward-looking uncertainty (future variants, government mandates), indicating that the hazard remains live two years after the WHO declaration.  Because the filing date (14 Feb 2022) is within three years of the event’s onset, the Time Decay Principle permits high severity scores.  Nevertheless, the company also discloses partial offsets (cost pass-throughs, cost-containment programs, full plant operations), which temper but do not eliminate the residual risk.  Overall, the narrative supports elevated—but not maximal—snippet scores in the 6-10 range, with minor downward adjustments where ON cites concrete mitigating actions.

evidence_list.snippet: The effects of the COVID-19 pandemic have had, and could continue to have, an adverse impact on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

components.reason: Explicit statement that impacts have already occurred ('have had').
Adds forward-looking dimension ('could continue'), showing ongoing exposure.
Covers three critical areas—business, operations, financial condition—indicating breadth of exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Past and future adverse impacts across key dimensions make this a high-severity, recent-event disclosure.

evidence_list.snippet: Our business has been, and is expected to continue to be, adversely impacted by the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Affirms historical adverse impact on the business.
Projects continuing impact, reinforcing persistence of risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct link to realised and continuing harm; slightly less granular than Snippet 1, hence marginally lower score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition to global macroeconomic effects, the COVID-19 pandemic and related adverse public health developments have been causing, and are expected to continue to cause, disruption to our domestic and international operations and sales activities.

components.reason: Describes actual ongoing disruption to operations and sales.
Covers both domestic and international scope, enlarging exposure.
Forecasts continued disruption, adding forward-looking dimension.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specifies operational and sales disruptions globally—high severity but lacks quantified dollar impact.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, we and our suppliers, third-party distributors, sub-contractors and customers have been, and are expected to continue to be, disrupted by worker absenteeism, quarantines and restrictions on certain of our employees’ ability to perform their jobs, office and factory closures or restrictions, labor shortages, disruptions to ports and other shipping infrastructure, border closures or other travel or health-related restrictions.

components.reason: Lists multiple concrete disruption channels across the supply chain.
States disruptions have occurred ('have been').
Adds expectation of continued disruption.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highly detailed, multi-stakeholder, realised and continuing disruptions justify a maximum score within recent-event window.

evidence_list.snippet: Depending on the magnitude of such effects on our manufacturing activities or the operations of our suppliers, third-party distributors or sub-contractors, our supply chain, manufacturing and product shipments could be delayed, which could materially adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.

components.reason: Highlights risk of delays in supply chain and shipments—core revenue driver.
Uses 'materially adversely affect', signalling severity.
Links risk to manufacturing and supplier operations, underscoring vulnerability.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Material, supply-chain centred risk; forward-looking but without quantification keeps it below 9.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, any economic downturn or recession brought on by the COVID-19 pandemic or other disease outbreaks could adversely affect demand for our products and impact our results of operations and financial condition.

components.reason: Identifies macro-level demand shock as a potential outcome.
Links to results of operations and financial condition.
Conditional phrasing ('could') reduces immediacy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Presents plausible but contingent demand risk—moderate severity.

evidence_list.snippet: These effects, alone or taken together, could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, legal exposure, or financial condition.

components.reason: Aggregates multiple risks into a 'material adverse effect' statement.
Adds legal exposure dimension.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic summation of prior points—moderate weight without new specifics.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent of the COVID-19 pandemic’s effect on our operational and financial performance will depend on future developments, including the duration, spread and intensity of the pandemic, including resurgences in certain geographic areas as a result of new strains and variants, such as Delta and Omicron, the efficacy of vaccines, the speed of vaccine rollouts and the effect of vaccine mandates, if any, on our employees, all of which are uncertain and difficult to predict.

components.reason: Acknowledges uncertainty tied to variants and vaccine efficacy, signalling ongoing volatility.
Connects these uncertainties directly to operational and financial performance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking uncertainty around variants and vaccines produces moderate risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: While we are not able at this time to estimate the long-term effect of these factors on our business, the adverse impact on our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows has been, and could continue to be, material.

components.reason: Admits inability to quantify long-term impact—a red flag.
States impact has already been material across multiple financial metrics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Confession of material, ongoing impact and lack of visibility elevates severity.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has had, and continues to have, a significant impact around the world, prompting governments and businesses to take unprecedented measures including restrictions on travel, business operations and temporary closures of facilities.

components.reason: Places disruption in global, systemic context; references unprecedented restrictions.
Clarifies that impact is ongoing ('continues to have').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides macro backdrop of continuing restrictions—high but not company-specific quantification.

evidence_list.snippet: While the semiconductor industry conditions have resulted in increased costs throughout our supply chain, we have been able to pass a majority of such increases to our customers, which also contributed to higher revenue for 2021.

components.reason: Acknowledges cost pressure in supply chain due to pandemic environment.
Strong mitigation: cost pass-through to customers.
Notes beneficial impact on revenue, further offsetting risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Risk acknowledged but substantially mitigated; net residual risk is minimal.

evidence_list.snippet: We have taken, and continue to take, significant cost containment efforts, including, but not limited to, workforce reductions and reducing discretionary spending.

components.reason: Indicates proactive mitigation actions.
Implies underlying cost pressures tied to pandemic environment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Primarily reflects mitigation; residual pandemic-related cost risk is low.

evidence_list.snippet: While all our global manufacturing sites are currently operational, our facilities could be required to temporarily curtail production levels or temporarily cease operations based on government mandates due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Identifies possible forced shutdowns directly linked to government pandemic mandates.
Notes current full operations, partially mitigating immediacy.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential for mandated shutdowns is severe; present operations mitigate but do not eliminate risk.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Company’s operational and financial performance is uncertain and will depend on many factors outside the Company’s control, including the timing, extent, trajectory and duration of the pandemic, the emergence of new variants, the development, availability, distribution and effectiveness of vaccines and treatments, the imposition of protective public safety measures, and the impact of the pandemic on the global economy and demand for products.

components.reason: Emphasises uncontrollable external factors affecting operational and financial performance.
Highlights vaccine and variant uncertainty, reinforcing future volatility.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive list of uncontrollable variables adds to uncertainty—moderate-high risk.
